mcqs.question: A projectile is launched with initial speed v₀ at an angle θ above the horizontal. Which expression gives the horizontal component of the initial velocity?
mcqs.explanation: The horizontal component is obtained by multiplying the magnitude by the cosine of the launch angle: v₀ₓ = v₀ cosθ. Option A gives the vertical component, C is the ratio of vertical to horizontal, and D is not a standard component expression.

mcqs.question: Which of the following equations correctly represents the trajectory y(x) of a projectile launched from the origin with speed u at angle θ (neglecting air resistance)?

options.A: y = x tanθ - (g x²)/(2 u² cos²θ)
options.B: y = x tanθ + (g x²)/(2 u² cos²θ)
options.C: y = u sinθ t - (1/2) g t²

mcqs.answer: y = x tanθ - (g x²)/(2 u² cos²θ)
mcqs.explanation: Eliminating time t between x = u cosθ t and y = u sinθ t - (1/2) g t² yields y = x tanθ - (g x²)/(2 u² cos²θ). Option B has the wrong sign, C and D are the parametric forms, not the trajectory equation.

mcqs.question: A projectile is launched from ground level and lands at the same level. Which formula gives its total time of flight?
mcqs.explanation: The upward and downward journeys are symmetric; the time to reach the highest point is u sinθ/g, so total time is twice that, giving T = 2u sinθ/g. Options B, C, D misuse components or miss the factor of 2.

mcqs.question: A stone is projected with speed 20 m s⁻¹ at 30° above the horizontal. What is its maximum height (take g = 9.8 m s⁻²)?
mcqs.explanation: Maximum height H = u² sin²θ/(2g). Here sin30° = 0.5, so H = (400 × 0.25)/(19.6) ≈ 5.1 m. Option B is double, C is half, D is unrelated.

mcqs.question: A projectile is launched with speed 25 m s⁻¹ at 45° to the horizontal. Ignoring air resistance, what is its horizontal range? (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
mcqs.explanation: Range R = u² sin2θ/g. With θ = 45°, sin90° = 1, so R = 625/9.8 ≈ 63.8 m. The other options correspond to incorrect use of the formula or rounding errors.

mcqs.question: A projectile is at the highest point of its trajectory. Which component of its velocity is zero at that instant?
mcqs.explanation: At the apex the vertical motion momentarily stops, so the vertical component of velocity is zero while the horizontal component remains unchanged. Hence option B is correct.

mcqs.question: Two projectiles are launched from the same point with identical speed and angle, but one is twice as massive as the other. In vacuum, their horizontal ranges will be:

options.A: The same, because mass does not affect projectile motion
options.B: Different, the heavier one will travel farther
options.C: Different, the lighter one will travel farther
options.D: Impossible to determine without air resistance data

mcqs.answer: The same, because mass does not affect projectile motion
mcqs.explanation: In the absence of air resistance, projectile motion depends only on initial speed, angle, and gravity; mass cancels out of the equations. Therefore both have identical ranges. Options B and C reflect the common misconception that heavier objects travel farther, and D is irrelevant because the scenario explicitly neglects air resistance.

mcqs.question: A projectile is launched with speed 30 m s⁻¹ at an angle of 37° above the horizontal. What is the magnitude of its horizontal component (use cos 37° ≈ 0.80)?
mcqs.explanation: Horizontal component = v₀ cosθ = 30 × 0.80 ≈ 24 m s⁻¹. Option B ignores the angle, C corresponds to the vertical component (30 × 0.60), and D is unrelated.
